metadata.description: Returns a paginated list of tickets for the current tenant. Supports filtering by board, status, priority, client, assignee, category, open/closed/overdue flags, and entered/closed date ranges — see the parameters list for all available filters. For aggregate counts (e.g. how many tickets are open or high priority), prefer GET /api/v1/tickets/stats or set limit=1 and read pagination.total from the response. Use GET /api/v1/boards, GET /api/v1/statuses, and GET /api/v1/priorities for lookup data instead of sampling tickets. If you send the fields query parameter, use only these exact field names: ticket_id, ticket_number, title, status_id, status_name, status_is_closed, priority_name, assigned_to_name, client_name, contact_name, updated_at, entered_at, closed_at, latest_activity_at, tags, or mobile_list. Do not invent aliases such as id, subject, status, priority, client, created_at, or description. Use sort=latest_activity_at to order by the most recently active tickets.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Pagination page number (default 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of tickets per page (max 100, default 25). Set limit=1 when you only need pagination.total for an aggregate count.

parameters.name: board_id
parameters.description: Filter to a specific board.

parameters.name: board_name
parameters.description: Filter by board display name (case-sensitive exact match). Prefer board_id when you already have a UUID.

parameters.name: status_id
parameters.description: Filter by a single ticket status UUID.

parameters.name: status_ids
parameters.description: Filter by multiple status UUIDs as a comma-separated list (for example status_ids=uuid1,uuid2). Useful for matching several open or closed statuses at once.

parameters.name: status_name
parameters.description: Filter by status display name (case-sensitive exact match). Prefer status_id/status_ids when you already have UUIDs.

parameters.name: priority_id
parameters.description: Filter by ticket priority UUID. Call GET /api/v1/priorities to discover priority UUIDs.

parameters.name: priority_name
parameters.description: Filter by priority display name (case-sensitive exact match). Use this when the user asks for tickets of a specific priority like "High", "Highest", "Medium", or "Low" and you do not want to look up a UUID first.

parameters.name: category_id
parameters.description: Filter by ticket category UUID.

parameters.name: subcategory_id
parameters.description: Filter by ticket subcategory UUID.

parameters.name: category_name
parameters.description: Filter by category display name (case-sensitive exact match).

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Filter by client identifier.

parameters.name: client_name
parameters.description: Filter by client display name (case-sensitive exact match). Prefer client_id when you already have a UUID.

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: Filter by client location UUID.

parameters.name: contact_name_id
parameters.description: Filter by primary contact UUID on the ticket.

parameters.name: contact_name
parameters.description: Filter by contact display name (case-sensitive exact match).

parameters.name: assigned_to
parameters.description: Filter tickets assigned to a specific technician (user UUID).

parameters.name: entered_by
parameters.description: Filter tickets created by a specific user UUID.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Filter by ticket title (substring match).

parameters.name: ticket_number
parameters.description: Filter by ticket number (for example alga0001748).

parameters.name: is_open
parameters.description: When true, only open tickets are returned.

parameters.name: is_closed
parameters.description: When true, only closed tickets are returned.

parameters.name: has_assignment
parameters.description: When true, only tickets that have an assignee are returned; when false, only unassigned tickets.

parameters.name: response_state
parameters.description: Only tickets whose turn it is: awaiting_client (we replied, waiting on the client) or awaiting_internal (the client replied, waiting on us).

parameters.name: entered_from
parameters.description: Lower bound on entered_at as an ISO-8601 datetime (inclusive).

parameters.name: entered_to
parameters.description: Upper bound on entered_at as an ISO-8601 datetime (inclusive).

parameters.name: closed_from
parameters.description: Lower bound on closed_at as an ISO-8601 datetime (inclusive).

parameters.name: closed_to
parameters.description: Upper bound on closed_at as an ISO-8601 datetime (inclusive).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by (default entered_at). Only these values are accepted: ticket_number, title, entered_at, updated_at, closed_at, due_date, client_name, status_name, priority_name, latest_activity_at, plus created_at as a legacy alias for entered_at. latest_activity_at orders by the newest of the ticket's own timestamps and its newest visible comment. Any other value is rejected with a 400 error.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction (default desc). Ties break on ticket_id descending.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return. Use only these exact values: ticket_id, ticket_number, title, status_id, status_name, status_is_closed, priority_name, assigned_to_name, client_name, contact_name, updated_at, entered_at, closed_at, latest_activity_at, tags, or mobile_list. If you are not sure, omit fields entirely instead of guessing aliases.

parameters.name: field_ranges[description_html]
parameters.description: Optional UTF-8 byte range for the description_html field, formatted as start-end (for example 0-4095). When returned data is truncated, inspect meta.truncated_fields for continuation offsets.

latest_activity_at.description: Newest of the ticket's own timestamps and its newest visible comment. Returned when requested through fields.

examples.name: Sample recent tickets for reference data
examples.notes: Inspect the response payload to reuse board_id, status_id, priority_id, and assigned_to values that are known to be valid. Prefer fields=... to keep payloads compact, but only use the documented field names exactly as written. If you are unsure which field names are valid, omit fields instead of guessing. If you only need a single set of identifiers, take the first ticket in the data array that has non-null board_id, status_id, and priority_id and reuse those UUIDs for the new ticket.

metadata.description: Returns pre-computed ticket counts and metrics for the current tenant in a single call. Use this whenever the user asks aggregate questions like "how many tickets are open", "how many high priority tickets", "how many overdue tickets", or "how many tickets per board/status/priority/category". This endpoint returns totals grouped by status, priority, category, and board, plus counts of open/closed/overdue/unassigned tickets and tickets created today/this week/this month. Prefer this over paginating GET /api/v1/tickets and counting rows yourself.

data.description: Ticket statistics for the current tenant. Priority names (e.g. "High", "Medium") are the keys in tickets_by_priority and map directly to the priority_name values used by GET /api/v1/tickets.

total_tickets.description: Total number of tickets in the tenant, regardless of status.

open_tickets.description: Number of tickets that are currently open (status.is_closed = false).

closed_tickets.description: Number of tickets whose status is marked closed.

overdue_tickets.description: Number of open tickets past their due/SLA date.

unassigned_tickets.description: Number of open tickets with no assignee.

tickets_by_status.description: Map of status display name to ticket count, for example {"New": 42, "In Progress": 18, "Closed": 140}.

tickets_by_priority.description: Map of priority display name to ticket count, for example {"High": 12, "Highest": 3, "Medium": 55, "Low": 20}. These keys are the same strings accepted by the priority_name filter on GET /api/v1/tickets.

tickets_by_category.description: Map of category display name to ticket count.

tickets_by_board.description: Map of board display name to ticket count.

average_resolution_time.description: Average resolution time in hours across closed tickets, or null if there are no closed tickets.

examples.name: Answer "how many high priority tickets are open" in one call
examples.notes: Call this endpoint and read data.tickets_by_priority["High"] for the count of high-priority tickets. Note the map covers all tickets regardless of status — if the user asks specifically about OPEN high-priority tickets and you need to scope by status, fall back to GET /api/v1/tickets?is_open=true&priority_name=High&limit=1 and read pagination.total from that response.

metadata.description: Returns the full ticket record for a specific ticket. Prefer this over expanding list responses when you already know the ticket_id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: field_ranges[description_html]
parameters.description: Optional UTF-8 byte range for description_html, formatted as start-end (for example 0-4095). When returned data is truncated, inspect meta.truncated_fields for continuation offsets.

examples.name: Read one ticket in detail
examples.notes: Use this endpoint after a list/search call gives you a ticket_id. If description_html is large, fetch it in byte windows with field_ranges[description_html]=start-end instead of asking for a bigger list payload.

metadata.description: Creates a new ticket on a specified board with the desired status and priority. Requires the user to have ticket create permissions. Do not invoke this until you have gathered valid UUIDs for board_id, client_id, status_id, and priority_id from prior lookup calls. IMPORTANT: status_id must belong to the same board as board_id — use GET /api/v1/statuses?type=ticket&board_id=... to discover valid statuses for the chosen board. Set suppressContactNotifications=true to create the ticket silently — no customer-facing ticket-created email (which otherwise falls back to the client's address when the ticket has no contact) and no portal notifications. Add suppressInternalNotifications=true to also skip agent and watcher notifications; internal suppression requires customer suppression. Silent creations still create normal audit, workflow, and webhook records.

board_id.description: Ticket board identifier. Call GET /api/v1/boards to list available boards and pick a valid board_id. Always provide the UUID, never the board name, slug, or display label.

client_id.description: Owning client identifier. Retrieve clients via GET /api/v1/clients (supporting filters such as name or status) to resolve the correct client_id, and provide that UUID in the payload (do not send the client name).

status_id.description: Initial ticket status identifier. Call GET /api/v1/statuses?type=ticket&board_id=... to list valid statuses for the chosen board. The status_id MUST belong to the same board as board_id. Do not send a status label like "Open" or a field named "status".

priority_id.description: Ticket priority identifier. Use GET /api/v1/priorities or sample existing tickets to obtain a valid priority_id. Always include the UUID (never send fields named "priority" or the textual priority name).

contact_name_id.description: Primary contact for this ticket. Look up contacts through GET /api/v1/contacts (optionally filter by client_id) before supplying this reference.

location_id.description: Client location identifier. Call GET /api/v1/clients/{client_id}/locations to enumerate valid locations for the chosen client.

category_id.description: Ticket category identifier. Fetch categories via GET /api/v1/categories/ticket (filter by board_id if necessary) to resolve the correct category_id.

subcategory_id.description: Ticket subcategory identifier. After retrieving the category list or tree (GET /api/v1/categories/ticket or GET /api/v1/categories/ticket/tree/{board_id}), choose the desired subcategory_id.

assigned_to.description: Technician assignment. Use GET /api/v1/users (filtering by role, team, or name) to acquire the user_id of the assignee and submit that UUID.

tags.description: Optional labels to associate with the ticket. Discover existing tag values via GET /api/v1/tags or GET /api/v1/tags/search before reusing them.

suppressContactNotifications.description: Suppress the customer-facing ticket-created email and portal notifications for this creation. Use it for machine-generated tickets that should not reach the client.

suppressInternalNotifications.description: Also suppress agent and watcher email, in-app, and push notifications. Requires suppressContactNotifications=true.

examples.name: Create ticket example
examples.notes: Before calling this endpoint, resolve every referenced identifier by invoking the appropriate lookup APIs: GET /api/v1/boards to choose board_id, GET /api/v1/statuses?type=ticket&board_id=... to choose a status_id that belongs to that board, GET /api/v1/clients to choose client_id, GET /api/v1/contacts?client_id=... for contact_name_id, GET /api/v1/clients/{client_id}/locations for location_id, GET /api/v1/categories/ticket for category/subcategory options, GET /api/v1/users to select the assignee, and GET /api/v1/tags to reuse tag names. CRITICAL: status_id must belong to the same board as board_id — mismatched values will be rejected with a 400 error. Always send UUID fields exactly as documented — do not substitute human-readable names such as "High" or "In Progress," and do not introduce extra fields that are not part of this schema.

examples.name: Create an alert ticket without notifying the client
examples.notes: Contact suppression skips the customer-facing ticket-created email — which, with no contact_name_id, would otherwise go to the client's own address — and the portal notification. The assignee and internal watchers are still notified; add suppressInternalNotifications=true to silence them too.

metadata.summary: Update a ticket with optional silent-notification controls
metadata.description: Updates one or more ticket fields. Set suppressContactNotifications=true to avoid customer email and portal notifications for this operation. Set suppressInternalNotifications=true as well to also avoid agent and watcher notifications; internal suppression requires customer suppression. Silent updates still create normal audit, workflow, and webhook records. Do not hand-edit attributes.watch_list: it is a derived mirror, and any watch_list sent here is ignored and the stored list preserved. To copy contacts, users or external emails on updates use POST /tickets/{id}/watchers (and PATCH/DELETE on the same path).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

attributes.description: Free-form ticket attributes. Do not put watch_list here: it is ignored and the stored list preserved. Use POST/PATCH/DELETE /tickets/{id}/watchers.

suppressContactNotifications.description: Suppress customer-facing email and portal notifications for this update.

suppressInternalNotifications.description: Also suppress agent and watcher email, in-app, and push notifications. Requires suppressContactNotifications=true.

examples.name: Silently change ticket priority for everyone
examples.notes: The priority change remains visible in ticket history and webhooks, but no customer, agent, or watcher notification is sent.

metadata.description: Returns the comments attached to a ticket. Use small limits and field-scoped byte ranges when comment bodies are large.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of comments to return (1-200). Prefer small values when exploring ticket history.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based comment offset.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Comment sort order.

parameters.name: field_ranges[comment_text]
parameters.description: Optional UTF-8 byte range for comment_text, formatted as start-end (for example 0-4095). Use meta.truncated_fields to continue fetching long comments.

parameters.name: field_ranges[comment_html]
parameters.description: Optional UTF-8 byte range for comment_html, formatted as start-end (for example 0-4095).

examples.name: Read recent comments with ranged comment text
examples.notes: Prefer this endpoint over large ticket list payloads when the user asks for comment history or long comment bodies.

metadata.summary: Add a comment to a ticket
metadata.description: Adds a client or internal comment to the specified ticket. Silent flags suppress the comment notification without hiding the comment from ticket history, workflows, or webhooks.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

is_internal.description: When true, records the comment as internal only.

is_resolution.description: When true, marks the comment as a resolution.

parent_comment_id.description: Optional parent comment for a threaded reply.

time_spent.description: Optional time (in minutes) to log with the comment.

suppressContactNotifications.description: Suppress customer-facing notification delivery for this comment.

suppressInternalNotifications.description: Also suppress agent and watcher notifications for this comment. Requires suppressContactNotifications=true.

cc.description: One-off Cc recipients for this comment's email only. They are never added to the ticket watch list and receive no later comments. Not allowed with is_internal. Max 20 cc + bcc combined.

bcc.description: One-off Bcc recipients for this comment's email only. Never returned to client-portal callers. Not allowed with is_internal. Max 20 cc + bcc combined.

metadata.summary: List time entries logged on a ticket
metadata.description: Returns an authorization-aware summary of the time logged on a ticket. Each entry is evaluated through the authorization kernel against `time_entry:read`; the caller always sees their own entries, plus any other users' entries the kernel allows (e.g. team members managed by the caller, or entries permitted by an assigned authorization bundle). Entries the caller cannot see are still counted toward an anonymized aggregate (`othersHiddenCount` + `othersHiddenMinutes`) so that totals stay accurate without leaking individual entries.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

entries.description: Visible time entries — always includes the caller's own entries; includes other users' entries that the authorization kernel allows for the caller (e.g. via team management or an authorization bundle).

ownTotalMinutes.description: Total billable minutes logged by the calling user.

othersTotalMinutes.description: Total billable minutes logged by other users (always populated, even when individual entries are hidden).

othersEntryCount.description: Total count of entries logged by other users (always populated).

othersVisibleMinutes.description: Subset of `othersTotalMinutes` for entries the caller is authorized to see in `entries`.

othersVisibleCount.description: Subset of `othersEntryCount` for entries the caller is authorized to see in `entries`.

othersHiddenMinutes.description: Remaining minutes from other users' entries that the caller is not authorized to see; surfaced as an anonymized aggregate.

othersHiddenCount.description: Remaining count of other users' entries that the caller is not authorized to see; surfaced as an anonymized aggregate.

examples.name: Read time logged on a ticket
examples.notes: Use this endpoint to render time-tracking summaries on the ticket detail page or in mobile clients without paging through the global timesheet list.

metadata.summary: List external links for a ticket
metadata.description: Returns structured references from the ticket to records in external systems (Discord, Slack, GitHub, Jira, email, custom systems). Each entry carries the registry key, external id, realm, relationship (origin/mirror/reference), actor, and a resolved display object with a readable label and link-out href. The origin link, when present, is how the ticket arrived in Alga.

metadata.summary: Add an external link to a ticket
metadata.description: Creates an external-system reference for a ticket. Defaults to a ticket-level link; set entity_type to 'comment' with a comment_id to attach the reference to one of the ticket's comments. Only one origin link per entity is permitted; a duplicate external record is rejected. Provide an http(s) url when the system has no URL template. Use GET /api/v1/tickets/by-external-link to find an existing ticket for the same external record before creating one.
Updates mutable fields on an existing link belonging to the ticket: relationship, url, actor, external_status, external_updated_at, last_synced_at, and metadata. system and external_id are immutable.

metadata.summary: Remove an external link from a ticket
metadata.description: Deletes a link belonging to the ticket and records a ticket activity entry. Any inbound integration that relies on the link for deduplication should stop using it after removal.

metadata.summary: Find a ticket by its external record
metadata.description: Returns the ticket and matching link for a system/external_id pair, with an optional external_parent_id for comment-level records. Returns 404 when no ticket carries the external record. Use this as the dedupe check before creating a ticket from an external source.

metadata.summary: List ticket watchers: who is copied or cc'd on a ticket's updates
playbooks: See who is copied or cc'd on ticket updates: list the ticket watchers.
metadata.description: Watchers vs. additional agents vs. comment cc: WATCHERS (these endpoints) are the persistent watch list - client contacts, internal users or any bare external email - copied on ticket updates until removed; they can be added silently. ADDITIONAL AGENTS (/tickets/{id}/agents) are internal staff working the ticket only; never use them for external people. COMMENT CC/BCC is a one-off copy of a single comment email and never joins the watch list. Use this for requests like 'cc X on updates', 'copy X on this ticket', 'notify X when it changes', 'add to the watch list', 'add a watcher', 'add an external contact / external email'. Returns the current watch list of the ticket, including paused (active=false) watchers. A change to the watch list is not itself emailed to anyone: the new watcher is simply copied on later ticket updates. Unless silent=true the write publishes one ticket-updated event with no field changes; it creates no watcher email, but it does create the generic 'ticket updated' in-app notification for the assigned agents and the client-portal contact. silent=true sets suppressContactNotifications and suppressInternalNotifications on that event, which skips those in-app notifications (request-scoped, never stored); use it when the change should leave no trace for staff or the customer. Every response is the full list of watchers: {email, name, active, entity_type, entity_id, source}; email (case-insensitive) is the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

examples.name: See who is watching a ticket
examples.notes: Read data[] for each watcher; check email before adding to avoid redundant calls (adds are idempotent anyway).

metadata.summary: Add a ticket watcher: copy or cc a contact, user or external email on ticket updates
playbooks: Copy, cc or notify a client contact, internal user or external email on ticket updates: POST the watcher endpoint with contact_id, user_id or email.
Add an external watcher or external email to a ticket: use the watcher endpoint, not additional agents (internal staff only) and not comment cc (one comment only).
Example: to copy Dorothy Gale and an outside mailbox on updates, POST once with her contact_id and once with the mailbox email.
metadata.description: Watchers vs. additional agents vs. comment cc: WATCHERS (these endpoints) are the persistent watch list - client contacts, internal users or any bare external email - copied on ticket updates until removed; they can be added silently. ADDITIONAL AGENTS (/tickets/{id}/agents) are internal staff working the ticket only; never use them for external people. COMMENT CC/BCC is a one-off copy of a single comment email and never joins the watch list. Use this for requests like 'cc X on updates', 'copy X on this ticket', 'notify X when it changes', 'add to the watch list', 'add a watcher', 'add an external contact / external email'. Provide exactly one of contact_id (client contact), user_id (internal user) or email (any mailbox, e.g. an external address). The contact/user is resolved to its email and name server-side; an unknown or other-tenant id, or one without an email, returns 422. Idempotent set-add: an email already on the list is re-activated, never duplicated. Example: to copy Dorothy Gale (a client contact) and an outside mailbox on updates, call this once with her contact_id and once with {"email":"ops@vendor.example"}. A change to the watch list is not itself emailed to anyone: the new watcher is simply copied on later ticket updates. Unless silent=true the write publishes one ticket-updated event with no field changes; it creates no watcher email, but it does create the generic 'ticket updated' in-app notification for the assigned agents and the client-portal contact. silent=true sets suppressContactNotifications and suppressInternalNotifications on that event, which skips those in-app notifications (request-scoped, never stored); use it when the change should leave no trace for staff or the customer. Every response is the full list of watchers: {email, name, active, entity_type, entity_id, source}; email (case-insensitive) is the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

contact_id.description: Client contact to watch. Exactly one of contact_id, user_id, email.

user_id.description: Internal user to watch. Exactly one of contact_id, user_id, email.

email.description: Any bare email address, including external mailboxes. Exactly one of contact_id, user_id, email.

name.description: Optional display name, used only when the watcher has none yet.

silent.description: Request-scoped, never stored. true = send no customer or internal notification for this write.

examples.name: Copy a client contact on updates
examples.notes: Persistent watch-list entry; the contact's email and name are resolved server-side.

examples.name: Copy an external mailbox silently
examples.notes: Adds the watcher without notifying anyone about the change itself; the mailbox receives future ticket updates.

metadata.summary: Pause or resume a ticket watcher (cc on updates) without removing it
playbooks: Pause or resume a watcher: PATCH with email and active=false or true.
metadata.description: Watchers vs. additional agents vs. comment cc: WATCHERS (these endpoints) are the persistent watch list - client contacts, internal users or any bare external email - copied on ticket updates until removed; they can be added silently. ADDITIONAL AGENTS (/tickets/{id}/agents) are internal staff working the ticket only; never use them for external people. COMMENT CC/BCC is a one-off copy of a single comment email and never joins the watch list. Use this for requests like 'cc X on updates', 'copy X on this ticket', 'notify X when it changes', 'add to the watch list', 'add a watcher', 'add an external contact / external email'. Identifies the watcher by email (case-insensitive) and toggles active. A paused watcher stays on the list but is not copied. Returns 404 if the email is not a watcher. A change to the watch list is not itself emailed to anyone: the new watcher is simply copied on later ticket updates. Unless silent=true the write publishes one ticket-updated event with no field changes; it creates no watcher email, but it does create the generic 'ticket updated' in-app notification for the assigned agents and the client-portal contact. silent=true sets suppressContactNotifications and suppressInternalNotifications on that event, which skips those in-app notifications (request-scoped, never stored); use it when the change should leave no trace for staff or the customer. Every response is the full list of watchers: {email, name, active, entity_type, entity_id, source}; email (case-insensitive) is the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

active.description: false pauses updates, true resumes them.

silent.description: Request-scoped, never stored. true = send no customer or internal notification for this write.

examples.name: Pause a watcher
examples.notes: The watcher remains listed with active=false.

metadata.summary: Remove a ticket watcher so they are no longer copied or cc'd on updates
playbooks: Stop copying or cc'ing someone on ticket updates: DELETE the watcher with ?email=.
metadata.description: Watchers vs. additional agents vs. comment cc: WATCHERS (these endpoints) are the persistent watch list - client contacts, internal users or any bare external email - copied on ticket updates until removed; they can be added silently. ADDITIONAL AGENTS (/tickets/{id}/agents) are internal staff working the ticket only; never use them for external people. COMMENT CC/BCC is a one-off copy of a single comment email and never joins the watch list. Use this for requests like 'cc X on updates', 'copy X on this ticket', 'notify X when it changes', 'add to the watch list', 'add a watcher', 'add an external contact / external email'. Removes the watcher whose email matches the ?email= query parameter (optional &silent=true). Returns 404 when that email is not a watcher. A change to the watch list is not itself emailed to anyone: the new watcher is simply copied on later ticket updates. Unless silent=true the write publishes one ticket-updated event with no field changes; it creates no watcher email, but it does create the generic 'ticket updated' in-app notification for the assigned agents and the client-portal contact. silent=true sets suppressContactNotifications and suppressInternalNotifications on that event, which skips those in-app notifications (request-scoped, never stored); use it when the change should leave no trace for staff or the customer. Every response is the full list of watchers: {email, name, active, entity_type, entity_id, source}; email (case-insensitive) is the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email of the watcher to remove (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: silent
parameters.description: true = send no notification for this removal.

examples.name: Stop copying an external mailbox
examples.notes: Use this for the persistent watch list; comment cc needs no cleanup.

metadata.summary: Add an internal staff member (technician, coworker or colleague) as an additional agent; internal staff only
playbooks: Add another technician to this ticket: POST the agents endpoint with the internal user_id so a second agent can help work the ticket.
Add a coworker or colleague to help on a ticket, or assign additional staff as another agent: use the additional agents endpoint.
Add an additional agent to help work the ticket (internal staff only, never an external person).
metadata.description: Adds an INTERNAL user (staff) as an additional agent working the ticket and publishes the additional-agent-assigned event so notifications fire unless suppressed. Internal staff only: to copy an external person, client contact or bare email on updates, use POST /tickets/{id}/watchers instead; for a one-off copy of a single comment use the comment cc/bcc fields. A ticket with no primary agent promotes the user to primary. A duplicate returns 409.

Multipart/form-data upload only; this endpoint cannot be called through call_api_endpoint, which sends JSON. To attach a file to a ticket, use the attach_file tool or POST /api/v1/documents (entity_type ticket) instead.
